headline: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed Bill 133, which would let more county properties be used for temporary living in vehicles; no legislative action was taken.
meeting.recap: The committee discussed Bill 133 (2026), which amends Chapter 10.76 of the Maui County Code.[[0:04:59]] The bill would let more county properties be used for temporary living in vehicles.[[0:07:37]] This was a Rule 7B discussion, so no legislative action was taken.[[0:08:01]] A deputy corporation counsel (county attorney) said the changes allow living in vehicles 24 hours a day, not only 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.[[0:16:00]] A testifier said the proposed site has no stores or gas stations nearby.[[0:28:12]] Another testifier asked the council to slow down and work with the people who will use the program.[[0:35:43]] The director said the site will have private security around the clock.[[1:01:23]] The director expects to serve 50 to 60 people.[[1:12:30]] If the bill passes Friday and the site is finished this week, moving people could start next week.[[1:21:56]] The pilot is expected to run six months at first.[[1:29:29]] A separate permanent safe parking site in Kahului is still moving forward.[[1:41:12]] Detailed liability questions would need an executive session (a closed-door discussion) or private calls before Friday.[[2:14:17]]
decided: Public testimony was closed with no objections.
meeting.next: The chair said the bill will get non-substantive (wording-only) cleanup for Friday. Members can call the deputy corporation counsel with liability questions before Friday. The public can email site or program ideas to the director at director.hc@co.maui.hi.us. The director said she will tell members when the security agreement is finalized.

moments.q: Director explains when the temporary site could open
"We will not be allowing people to remain in that area."

boards.name: Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

issues.oneLine: The county plans a temporary site for people now living in vehicles along the road.
issues.why: The director said the site aims to keep people safer, away from traffic and its danger.

deadlines.t: Start moving people to the temporary site.

issues.next: The bill is set for second and final reading on Friday.
issues.brief: The director expects the site to serve 50 to 60 people.[[#1]] The site will have private security 24 hours a day.[[#2]] The site will offer portable toilets, hand washing stations and drinking water.[[#3]] People who turn down all options will not be allowed to stay in the current roadside area.[[#4]]
